title: Fictitious forces in accelerating frames
canonical_question: What fictitious forces appear in a non-inertial (accelerating) reference frame?
summary: In an accelerating frame, objects seem to be pushed by forces that have no physical source.
Pressed back into your seat as a car accelerates, or flung outward on a roundabout, you feel such apparent forces.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Forces that come from the frame
sections.body_md: In an accelerating frame, objects seem to be pushed by forces that have no physical source. These are called fictitious or inertial forces, and they appear only because the frame itself is accelerating. In an inertial frame they vanish.

sections.heading: Familiar examples
sections.body_md: Pressed back into your seat as a car accelerates, or flung outward on a roundabout, you feel such apparent forces. Really you are just resisting the frame’s acceleration through your own inertia. Naming them helps calculation but they are not true interactions.

key_points: They have no physical source body.
They disappear in an inertial frame.
core.bridge_to_parent: It deepens the objective by contrasting inertial and non-inertial frames.

seeds: How do I switch back to an inertial frame?
